cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: Drift from partial landings of a multi-surface change. Caught at git commit-boundary + audit-time, never write-time.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Atomic lockstep (documentary)
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: R-37 (atomic lockstep) is DOCUMENTARY across the entire governance surface — there is NO write-time DENY, by design. A PreToolUse hook sees exactly one file per call and cannot inspect a multi-file commit set. Enforcement = git's commit-boundary atomicity + the librarian governance-parity-audit capability at session-close. The lockstep set = pillar JSON + narrative spoke + CLAUDE.md.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: Ossify (advisory forever) or promote without data.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Stage-gated promotion framework
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: Tier 1 advisory + promotion_criterion. Clean data -> promote to a blocking tier; no data -> retire. Stage-gated promotion, never ossify, never promote without data.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: Over-reach (auto-overwriting semantic content) or under-reach (failing to auto-fix mechanical drift).
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Self-healing boundary
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: Mechanical drift auto-fixes (librarian regenerates mechanically-derivable values); semantic drift self-flags for review, never auto-overwritten.

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh write-time DENY on shadowing writes missing `_override_reason`
version-control merge-conflict surfacing on foundation upgrades touching shadowed entries
cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: Silent collisions between adopter customization and foundation canonical produce unpredictable runtime behavior — rules with the same ID compete; overlay edits silently disable foundation rules.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Layer-3 Overlay Collision Tiebreaker
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: When adopter Layer-3 overlay and foundation canonical both declare the same rule ID or extensible entry kind: adopter Layer-3 SHADOWS foundation (adopter wins). Foundation declaration is preserved but does not fire. Adopter MUST carry `_override_reason` (free-text, mandatory) on every shadowing entry. Write-time DENY on shadowing writes without `_override_reason`; per-write `--force-override` bypass; no persistent disable.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: A write to a known-retired path lands silently. Empty tripwire_paths at ship means no-op by default.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Dead-path tripwire
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: Writes to a declared dead path are DENIED. Ships with an EMPTY tripwire_paths[] (no dead paths declared at v1.0.0); the mechanism is present for adopters/future use.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: A skill changes without the cross-surface propagation protocol.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Skill-change protocol
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: Editing a skill (SKILL.md / process.sh) surfaces the change-protocol checklist (save memory, update docs, grep downstream). Advisory.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: librarian-manifest.json drifts stale against the real foundation surface.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: The librarian-manifest read-replica is audited for staleness against the foundation surface. Audit-tier (librarian), not write-time.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: Escape hatches used routinely rather than exceptionally; governance silently eroded.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Bypass/override abuse audit
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: Bypass/override usage (governance escape hatches, --force flags, bypass env vars) is audited for abuse patterns. Audit-tier (librarian).

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: claude-mem SessionEnd hook disabled; auto-memory silently stops persisting.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Protected SessionEnd hooks
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: Edits that would disable the claude-mem SessionEnd hook are DENIED (CLAUDE_MEM_DISABLE_OK=1 escape hatch). Load-bearing for auto-memory.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: A long session compacts without a fresh checkpoint; session continuity state is lost.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Checkpoint freshness gate
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: At context pressure thresholds, a fresh per-session checkpoint is required; the Stop hook gates until the checkpoint is fresh (< 10 min). Safety valve preserved above the high-pressure ceiling.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: Files touched in a session drift from their governed shape without surfacing.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Touched-file drift scan
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: On Stop, touched files are scanned for drift and surfaced advisorily.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: The default session-wiring loop is broken or mis-ordered; coordination + context-injection degrade.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Default session-register hook loop
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: The default SessionStart hook loop (session-register -> track-vault-write -> prompt-context) wires the multi-session coordination + context-injection band. Advisory framing.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: Memory files without frontmatter are mis-indexed in MEMORY.md / mis-resolved by retrieval.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: Memory-file frontmatter
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: Memory files (memory/<topic>.md) carry the required frontmatter shape (description/tags). Advisory.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: _index.md plan-index drifts stale against the real plans-tree.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: plan-index staleness audit
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: The librarian plan-index read-replica is audited for staleness against the plans-tree. Audit-tier.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: A bash-4 construct ships in a wrapper/hook and fails on the macOS default bash 3.2.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: cron-wrapper bash-3.2
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: cron wrappers + shipped hook bodies must be bash-3.2 clean (no associative arrays, no bash-4 builtins, no param-expansion case-conversion). DENY on violation.

cross_cutting_meta_rules.failure_mode: An auto-commit silently fails; expected state never lands in git.
cross_cutting_meta_rules.name: auto-commit silent-failure
cross_cutting_meta_rules.rule_text: Auto-commit silent-failure is detected + surfaced (now default-on). Advisory.

_rules.failure_mode: An upstream doc changes but its declared downstream mirrors drift. Advisory only — vault-writer fan-out is the forward path; R-54 is the thin/legacy cascade rail kept for the registry-declared edges.
_rules.rule_text: When an upstream document declared in this registry's entries[]/entities[] is edited, its declared downstream consumers/mirrors should be cascaded. ADVISORY — surfaced at write-time and at librarian session-close; never a write-time DENY. R-54 is the canonical doc-dep cascade ID; the hook header label is R-54 (renamed from R-07).

doc_dependencies.description: Documentation dependency registry. Hand-editable source of truth. Read by pre-write-guard.sh and librarian session-close. Mirrored into Logs/librarian-manifest.json -> doc_dependencies on each /librarian full run. Cascade registry consumed by pre-write-guard.sh + librarian session-close. The entities{} block is a declarative entity-mirror registry; per-type parity is enforced independently by trinity-drift-detect (plan) + memory-hygiene (memory); no generic entity-parity capability ships.

entities._comment: Entity parity registry. Each entity declares a canonical source path template with {name} placeholder, an instance-enumerator (glob/file-list/directory-index), the canonical field to compare, and mirrors with strict/presence-only flags. Declarative entity-mirror registry; per-type parity enforced independently by trinity-drift-detect (plan) + memory-hygiene (memory); no generic entity-parity capability ships.

section_semantics.Consequences: What becomes easier and what becomes harder as a result — including follow-on work, accepted trade-offs, and anything a superseding ADR would need to revisit.

section_semantics.Decision: The decision made, stated in active voice ('We will …'). One decision per ADR.

enforcement_layer: governance/frontmatter-rules.json `types` (type allowlist + per-type required/optional field declarations)
_rules.failure_mode: Files written with an unknown `type:` value or with missing Strict-tier required fields drift the schema contract silently. Downstream consumers (auto-routing, librarian, scaffold) cannot reason about the file because the contract has been violated. Without write-time DENY, the schema becomes documentation rather than enforcement — production-scale untagged-file backlogs (~500 files observed in a reference deployment) accumulate before audit catches up. The Tier 2 DENY closes the gap at the moment of capture, returning a structured error that enumerates the missing fields and points to the schema entry.
_rules.retired_types_handling: Files declaring a retired `type:` value (currently `engagement`, `project`) are DENIED with the retirement reference and `replacement` guidance pointing the author to the folder-lineage convention (field-level propagation via `engagement:` + `project:` frontmatter fields plus matching tags). See `retired_types` block.
_rules.rule_text: Every Strict-tier vault write MUST declare a `type:` value drawn from the governance/frontmatter-rules.json `types` allowlist (21 canonical type entries; 2 retired types preserved in `retired_types`). For Strict-tier files, the universal required fields (`type`, `tags`, `updated`) AND the per-type `required` field list MUST all be present in the YAML frontmatter. Pre-write-guard DENIES writes failing either check; the DENY message enumerates the missing fields plus the pillar entry path. Adding a new type or extending a required-field list requires R-37 atomic lockstep updating this pillar + the narrative spoke + pre-write-guard SCHEMA_KEY case + post-write-verify type_map in one commit. Standard-tier writes emit a warning instead of DENY (operator triages via librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit); Minimal-tier writes proceed without validation.

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh folder-placement advisory branch (Tier 1; never blocks)
_rules.failure_mode: Files written outside the canonical folder for their declared `type:` produce structural drift that compounds — the file is invisible to type-scoped queries, lives in a folder that does not match its archetype, and creates the impression that 'this type lives anywhere.' Once the precedent lands, follow-on writes drift further. The Tier 1 advisory fires at write-time rather than waiting for weekly audit so the operator sees the misplacement at the moment of capture and can move the file before publishing wikilinks.
_rules.rule_text: Files declaring a `type:` value SHOULD reside under the canonical folder for that type per governance/frontmatter-rules.json `path_routing` (the per-archetype lineage rules). Pre-write-guard emits a Tier 1 advisory `[R-33 FOLDER PLACEMENT]` when the file's path does not match the type's expected folder pattern. The advisory never blocks — engagement-specific exceptions, cross-engagement reference docs, and adopter-customized folder structures are legitimate causes for divergence. The advisory text enumerates the expected folder pattern and the current path so the author can decide. Persistent advisory firings on the same type/folder pair surface as `placement-drift` findings in the librarian audit.

_rules._enforcement_layer_note: R-37 is documentary, not write-time-enforced. There is no `pre-write-guard.sh atomic-lockstep branch (DENY on partial-surface writes)` — PreToolUse sees one file per invocation and cannot inspect a multi-file commit set; and no `git pre-commit hook` ships with the foundation. Enforcement is git's commit-boundary atomicity (commits are atomic by construction) + author discipline at the close-out merge boundary + the librarian governance-parity-audit at audit-time.
coupled_surfaces: governance/foundation-master.json (forward; built from this pillar via tools/build-foundation-master.sh)
_rules.failure_mode: Schema-touching changes that land in one surface without the others produce silent drift — the pillar declares a new type the hook does not recognize; the narrative spoke documents fields the pillar has not added; the rule registry references a field name the pillar spells differently. Within weeks the surfaces diverge enough that no single artifact is authoritative. Drift is detectable but already-broken when the audit surfaces it. R-37's structural commitment is that partial-surface commits are treated as the error they are; the close-out merge boundary and the librarian audit are the regression checks that catch drift before it ossifies.
_rules.rule_text: The frontmatter pillar binds three coupled surfaces under R-37 atomic lockstep: (1) governance/frontmatter-rules.json (canonical pillar declaring types, tiers, path-routing rules, and rule registry; absorbed the former schemas/vault-schema.json), (2) onboarding/scaffold/vault-architecture/Vault Architecture - Frontmatter.md (narrative spoke), (3) hooks/pre-write-guard.sh SCHEMA_KEY case-statement + hooks/post-write-verify.sh type_map (runtime mirror). Adding, modifying, or retiring a `type:` value, changing a required-field list, introducing a new field class, or updating the tier-compliance contract requires touching ALL THREE surfaces in a single commit. R-37 is documentary — enforced via author discipline at the close-out merge boundary, git's commit-boundary atomicity, and the librarian governance-parity-audit at audit-time. There is no write-time hook branch that denies partial-surface commits (PreToolUse architecture sees one file per invocation and has no view of the multi-file commit set; the proper enforcement layer for that would be a pre-commit or post-merge audit, not pre-write-guard). This entry is the pillar-scoped instantiation of the canonical R-37 meta-rule at governance/_index.json `cross_cutting_meta_rules[]`. The interim coupled-surfaces declaration in governance/_index.json carries hooks/config/gate-config.json (interim) and governance/foundation-master.json (forward).

enforcement_layer: post-write-verify.sh provides-presence advisory (Tier 1; combined with R-38 blockquote-summary block)
exemptions: Archive/** — archived content; provides-declaration is structurally unnecessary
Daily/** — daily notes are temporally-scoped, not capability-scoped
Logs/** — machine-emitted log surfaces; lifecycle is closed at write-time
Inbox/** — aggregation surfaces; provides lives at the canonical destination, not the staging copy
_rules.failure_mode: Long-form files (>200 lines) without a `provides:` declaration become opaque to consumers that route by capability rather than by path. The router cannot determine what concepts the file is canonical for; the librarian cannot detect provides-canonicality drift (R-40) because there is no claim to compare against; downstream agents loading the file have no fast way to decide whether the content is relevant. The advisory surfaces the omission at write-time so the author either declares `provides:` deliberately or accepts the file as content-only.
_rules.rule_text: Files exceeding 200 lines SHOULD declare a `provides:` array in their YAML frontmatter enumerating the concepts, rules, or capabilities the file is the canonical source for. Post-write-verify emits a Tier 1 advisory `[R-39 PROVIDES PRESENCE]` when a file over the line threshold lacks `provides:` or has `provides: []`. The advisory never blocks — content-only long-form files (raw transcripts, archive imports, daily-note dumps) are legitimate and the author can ignore the advisory. The librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit tracks recurring R-39 firings as `provides-coverage-drift` findings so the operator can triage at session-close.

enforcement_layer: drift-allowlist override at hooks/config/drift-allowlist.json (`provides_overlap[]` for deliberate co-canonical pairs)
_rules.failure_mode: Two or more canonical-scope files claiming the same `provides:` capability fragment authority. A consumer routing to the capability does not know which file to read; updates to one canonical do not propagate to the other; the two files drift into mutually-contradictory statements within months. Without an audit, the drift is invisible — `grep provides:` returns both files and the consumer picks one by accident. The librarian-audit finding surfaces the collision and asks the operator to either consolidate, archive one source, or register the overlap as deliberate in the drift-allowlist.
_rules.rule_text: Within the canonical-scope of the vault (vault root depth-1 + System Governance/** + Skills/**), no two files SHOULD declare the same capability in their `provides:` array. The librarian frontmatter-coverage-audit walks every Standard- and Strict-tier file's `provides:` declaration, builds an inverted index, and emits a `provides-canonicality-drift` finding whenever a capability is claimed by 2+ canonical-scope owners. Severity is `blocking` when any owner sits at vault root or inside System Governance/**; `warning` otherwise. Engagement reference docs, meeting notes, project context files, and daily notes are EXCLUDED from canonical-scope — `provides:` is project-scoped vocabulary there, not vault-wide canonical. Deliberate co-canonical pairs (e.g., a research packet plus its consumer-rendered spoke) register at hooks/config/drift-allowlist.json `provides_overlap[].capability` with rationale + audit-trail entry; allowlist entries mirror into librarian-manifest.json on every run and suppress the finding.

_rules.rule_text: Logs/ is a free-write scratch sink; write-time governance is AUTO-APPLIED (never denied, never propose-and-confirm). _memory_md_cap.enforcement_mechanism: advisory — hooks/pre-write-guard.sh emits additionalContext warning at write-time when any threshold exceeded; never blocks the write. The byte cap is the governing trigger.

line_count_method._note: Count BOTH the raw line count AND the comment-stripped line count, and gate on the LARGER of the two until MEMORY.md comment-stripping is empirically verified — HTML-comment blocks (<!-- -->) must not buy unlimited headroom. memory-consolidation-run.sh Check 8 implements this.

overflow_routing._description: Cold-spill seam — DOCUMENTED ONLY (pre-built, cheap). At byte-cap approach, relocate the COLDEST non-episodic entries to an on-demand MEMORY-archive.md and leave one pointer line in the index. DO NOT create MEMORY-archive.md until needed (auto-spill is v-next, volume-gated, no calendar gate). The fixed section order below makes the cold boundary always knowable.
overflow_routing.fixed_section_order_note: Schema-derived 1:1 from memory-schema.json type enum; most-loaded-first. The cold boundary for overflow routing is always the tail of the coldest non-episodic section (Procedural, then Semantic); Episodic is the SAMPLED windowed section (newest ~10 + a glob memory/episode_*.md pointer) and is not cold-spilled.

_memory_md_cap.rationale: Anthropic-documented at code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: the first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Entries past the cap silently drop. Advisory makes the truncation risk visible at write-time. MEMORY.md = index/read-replica; per-topic detail lives in memory/<file>.md referenced via [[wikilinks]]. The byte cap is the governing trigger (bites at ~110 entries before the line cap).
_memory_md_cap.scope: MEMORY.md under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ MUST stay within the Anthropic-documented load contract: first 200 lines OR first 25KB (whichever first) loaded at session start; entries past the cap silently drop. Per-line <= 200 chars (drift signal).

thresholds._governing_trigger_note: The BYTE cap is the governing trigger — it bites first (at ~110 entries) before the line cap. R-59 consumers gate on the byte ratio primarily; the line + char-line caps are secondary drift signals.

_rules.failure_mode: Unbounded backlog rows accrete session narrative inline; the index becomes a log; scan-readability collapses. Skill-enforced (backlog-hygiene), never write-time.
_rules.rule_text: Backlog row size is bounded — a row in the unified _backlog.md carries only a current-state pointer; session history lives in the satellite, not the row. backlog-hygiene flags over-long rows.

_rules.failure_mode: Drift between row and satellite; history scattered. Skill-enforced (backlog-hygiene), never write-time.
_rules.rule_text: Backlog sentinel pattern — the row carries the current-state pointer; the satellite at the plan dir / handoff.md is the single source of session history. backlog-hygiene validates the pattern.

_rules.failure_mode: Hand-edits inside sentinel regions are clobbered on regen, or stale regions diverge. Skill-enforced (backlog-hygiene), never write-time.
_rules.rule_text: Backlog sentinel pattern (companion to R-30) — sentinel-bounded row regions are librarian-regenerated; operator narrative is preserved outside the sentinels. backlog-hygiene validates parity.

_rules.failure_mode: Undisposed backlog rows float indefinitely; the GTD review loop has nothing to act on. Skill-enforced (backlog-hygiene), never write-time.
_rules.rule_text: Every backlog row (idea note or {researching,planned} manifest) carries a disposition signal (FIX NOW / ABSORB / STANDALONE / DEFERRED). backlog-hygiene escalates severity Warning -> Alert by stale_for_days against backlog_row.stale_advisory_days when a disposition is missing.

_rules.failure_mode: A master's sub_plans[] read-replica goes stale against the subs' real status; the master shows a sub as in-progress that has actually verified (or vice-versa); orchestration decisions read a phantom aggregate. Cross-file -> reconciler at session-close, never a blocking write-time path.
_rules.rule_text: Master sub_plans[] aggregation-integrity: the master manifest's sub_plans[].status read-replica MUST agree with each sub-plan's real published status. Cross-file invariant enforced by the librarian reconciler (NOT write-time) — extends trinity-drift-detect.sh / drift-sweep.sh with the master<->sub aggregation axis; detects (and optionally --fix) drift.

_rules.failure_mode: A sub-plan fails to publish a status transition, or attempts to write the master aggregate directly, breaking the pull-based read-replica model. Cross-file -> reconciler at session-close.
_rules.rule_text: Sub-publishes-upward: a sub-plan publishes its status + graduation_timestamp upward to the master (the master reads them into sub_plans[]); a sub MUST NOT mutate the master aggregate directly. Cross-file invariant enforced by the librarian reconciler (NOT write-time).

_rules.failure_mode: A sub declares a direct dependency on a sibling sub, recreating the agent-teams peer model the orchestrator-worker model deliberately rejects (MAST coordination-failure class). Advisory drift finding at session-close.
_rules.rule_text: Sub-peer-isolation: a sub-plan manifest MUST NOT carry a dependencies edge to a sibling sub-plan — route through the master manifest (the orchestrator-worker invariant: workers report only to the orchestrator, never to each other). Surfaced as a librarian reconciler drift finding (advisory).

plans._status_model_note: Two object types, two vocabularies. (1) Plan manifests carry the ONE canonical 8-state `status` (lifecycle.status_enum below; on plan-manifest-schema.json :: status). (2) Inbox idea notes carry inbox.funnel_status_enum {new, triaged, briefed} — a DIFFERENT object type (a pre-plan idea note, not a plan manifest), NOT collapsed into the 8-state plan status. The inbox funnel is separate from the plan-status enum. backlog_row.status_enum is the documented union shown in the rendered _backlog.md view.

backlog_row._stale_advisory_days_note: [advisory_threshold, escalation_threshold] in days for a backlog row missing a disposition. backlog-index emits backlog-row-missing-disposition once per run; backlog-hygiene escalates severity Warning->Alert by stale_for_days against these thresholds (R-56).

decision_records._description: Per-plan ADR (Architecture Decision Record) ledger. Short, immutable, individually-addressable, supersession-tracked decision records. Optional: a plan with no recorded decisions has no decisions/ dir. Body-structure contract at governance/file-type-contracts/adr.md.json; manifest pointer array at schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: decision_records[].
decision_records.agent_reload_contract: On plan resume, load non-superseded ADRs via manifest.decision_records[] as the decision context — NOT spec-prose archaeology.
decision_records.immutability: An accepted ADR is immutable. A decision change creates a NEW ADR that supersedes the prior one (prior Status -> superseded-by-ADR-NN); never an in-place edit. Distinct from the spec.md append-amendment pattern.
decision_records.placement_rule: repo-tier (docs/decisions/, 4-digit) IFF the decision changes adopter-inherited foundation behavior; else plan-tier (<plan>/decisions/ADR-NN-<slug>.md, 2-digit).
decision_records.tooling: NONE (no adr-tools / log4brains). Markdown-in-git + librarian enumeration covers it; bundling violates minimum-viable.

inbox._description: Pre-plan idea capture surface. Lightweight per-idea notes at ~/.claude-plans/_inbox/<slug>.md — cheap capture, extended-form body that grows in place, hook-unblocked (lib/plan-path.sh::classify_plan_path returns is_plan=0 so R-27 prefix/status never fires). Rendered into the unified _backlog.md by librarian:backlog-index. Graduates to a full plan via the idea->plan promote path (migrates body -> 00-ideation-brief.md, scaffolds the NN- quartet, tombstones the note).
inbox._slug_pattern_note: Inbox notes have NO NN- numeric prefix (distinct from plan slugs). The prefix is assigned at graduation, not at capture — avoids prefix burn on discarded ideas.
inbox.body: free-form extended idea content (description / rationale / notes); grows in place across funnel stages until graduation

Enforced by the hooks/pre-write-guard.sh manifest-substance branch (matcher Edit|Write on **/manifest.json), rollout ask->deny.

closed_to_archived._parameter_note: Default N=3 librarian-cycle ticks since closed. NOT a calendar gate.

in-progress->completed._note: completed = human's claim that work is done

metadata_flow._description: Orchestrator-worker contract for first-class master/sub-plan structure. Maps onto Claude Code's subagent orchestrator-worker invariant: workers run in isolated contexts, report only to the orchestrator, and NEVER communicate with each other — the deliberate OPPOSITE of the agent-teams peer model. Master/sub aggregation is pull-based and DERIVED: the master sub_plans[] is a librarian-generated read-replica (same trust class as _index.md), NEVER hand-edited.
metadata_flow.aggregation_model: pull-based-derived-read-replica (librarian reconciler reads each sub's published status into the master's sub_plans[]; never hand-edited; same class as _index.md)

handoff.md at any depth (append-only session record)

validation.promotion_eligible: A status promotion to `verified` is eligible only through an actual validation pass (the R-46-cousin verdict gate; plan-manifest-schema.json). `verified` is machine-stamped, never human-set.

_rules.failure_mode: Near-match drift in system-utility dimensions fragments operational subtypes within weeks. Two runs of the same routine emit two different tag values (e.g., #log/backlog-hygiene vs #log/backlog-cleanup), and the user-side graph filter splits routine activity across variant spellings. The discipline restores stability: every routine activity uses the STABLE, canonical tag value registered at first emission, and the hook DENIES near-match drift.
_rules.rule_text: Tags within system-utility dimensions (#log/*, #status/*) must match a value registered in governance/log-subtype-registry.json. Near-match writes (Levenshtein distance <= 2 or substring containment of an existing canonical value) are DENIED with a 'did you mean #<dim>/<canonical>?' suggestion. Genuinely new subtypes register explicitly via the prompt-and-commit pattern at first emission. The discipline mirrors the canonical-tag-per-concept principle on the system-utility surface where LLM stochasticity would otherwise fragment the vocabulary.

_rules.exempt_path_semantics: positive-list — unenumerated top-level paths default to the advisory firing (NOT auto-exempt). Adding a new exempt path requires R-37 documentary lockstep updating this rule + pre-write-guard.sh + the narrative spoke (System Governance - Tagging.md) + foundation-master.json bundle composition (composed via tools/build-foundation-master.sh, never hand-edited).
_rules.failure_mode: Non-exempt files written without tags become orphans in Obsidian graph view — invisible to user-side queries even though the file is legible to Claude-side surfaces via frontmatter fields. Pre-write tag-presence advisory surfaces the omission at the moment of write rather than at the weekly audit, closing a ~7-day detection lag.
_rules.rule_text: Every non-exempt vault write MUST carry a non-empty `tags:` array in its frontmatter. Pre-write-guard emits a Tier 1 advisory ([R-47 TAG PRESENCE]) when the field is missing or empty (tags: []). Distinguishes 'missing' (no tags: line) vs 'empty' (line present, no items). Exempt paths are enumerated in this rule's `r47_exempt_paths` array — they cover archive surfaces, ideation-brief symlinks, machine-emitted scratch/build zones, and system infrastructure paths whose tag-absence is structurally legitimate. The librarian tag-coverage-audit walks the vault at audit time and surfaces longer-running orphans + near-miss patterns (#scope/decisions vs #scope/decision — one is likely a typo) as advisory findings the operator triages.
_rules.seed_taxonomy_exempt_paths_semantics: DEDICATED tag-TAXONOMY exempt-list — SEPARATE from r47_exempt_paths (which is the tag-PRESENCE exempt-list for R-47). The foundation ships its vault-init seed surface tagged with adopter-tier dimensions (#scope/reference on the six System Governance/*.md spokes, #system-governance on System Governance/_index.md, #vault-writers on Vault Writers/_index.md) that model good tagging for adopters; the foundation taxonomy itself ships user_facing_dimensions:[] BY DESIGN (taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions), so those seed tags are NOT members of the foundation allowlist and the tag-taxonomy membership arm flags them as 9 day-one violations. These two glob surfaces exempt EXACTLY those seeds from the tag-not-in-taxonomy membership check ONLY — seeds stay byte-unchanged, still obey the R-47 tag-PRESENCE rule (r47_exempt_paths untouched), and adopter-authored tags on non-exempt paths are unaffected. Composed deterministically to foundation-master.json#seed_taxonomy_exempt_paths_composed via tools/build-foundation-master.sh (never hand-edit the bundle). Forward note: _load_tag_prefixes() reads only FM_FOUNDATION_MASTER and does not yet union the adopter overlay-master taxonomy — until that union-read lands, exemption (not adopter-dimension-registration) is the correct minimum-viable closure.

enforcement_layer: librarian tag-coverage-audit (audit-time consolidation prompt at 80% threshold)
_rules.failure_mode: Cap-widening defeats the working-memory rationale silently. An adopter activates a new engagement, user-facing tag count approaches 25, and the path of least resistance is 'raise the cap to 30.' Past 25, decision fatigue produces variant-creation rather than canonical-term selection, the vocabulary fragments, and user-side recall collapses. The cap is structural, not aspirational — silent widening is rejected; deliberate Layer 3 override is supported with audit trail.
_rules.override_mechanism: Layer 3 overlay-master.json :: tagging_cap_override with rationale + audit-trail entry
_rules.rule_text: Total count of distinct values across user-facing dimensions (declared at runtime by union of foundation-master.tagging.taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions + overlay-master.tagging.taxonomy.user_facing_dimensions) MUST stay under 25. System-utility dimensions (log, status) are exempt — they are machine-emitted and governed by the log-subtype registry (R-05). The librarian tag-coverage-audit emits an advisory when user-facing usage approaches 80% of the cap (>= 20 active values), surfaces a consolidation prompt with retire-candidate recommendations, and requires deliberate Layer 3 override (`overlay-master.json :: tagging_cap_override` with rationale + audit-trail entry) before silent widening can proceed.
_rules.source: governance/tagging-rules.json :: _rules (SoT; 25-tag cap grounded in Forte/Dubois working-vocabulary research + Hedden faceted-classification literature + Adobe AEM and SharePoint enterprise CMS picklist patterns)

taxonomy._description: Faceted tag taxonomy (canonical authority). Foundation user_facing_dimensions ship [] empty — concrete user-facing dimensions belong to adopter overlay-master.tagging.taxonomy.dimension_prefixes + .user_facing_dimensions, populated by onboarding archetype seeds at install time. Foundation ships taxonomy SHAPE + system-utility dimensions (status, log) governed by log-subtype-registry. Runtime allowlist = foundation + overlay-master union.
